title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous page: U_1 = P^1 − {0,1,∞}. U_n is the (Z/n)^2 Galois étale cover given by the affine Fermat curve with its 3n points where xyz = 0 removed. Its compactification Û_n is the Fermat curve x^n + y^n = z^n, of genus g_n = 1 + n(n−3)/2 = (n−1)(n−2)/2 (formulas (369)-(370)). The Q-points of U_n are exactly the non-trivial solutions of Fermat's equation; the 3n removed cusps are the trivial ones (xyz = 0).

The previous page sets up the homotopy exact sequence (371): 1 → π1(U_{n,Q̄}) → π1(U_n) → Γ_Q → 1. By the anabelian 'yoga' (the section conjecture for affine hyperbolic curves), Q-points of U_n should correspond to the non-cuspidal sections of (371). Grothendieck characterises these as the sections whose image of Γ_Q^+ = Ker(χ: Γ_Q → Ẑ*) has trivial centraliser in π1(U_n). The idea is that cuspidal sections carry a commuting inertia Ẑ(1).

This page draws two consequences.
(1) If Fermat is true for U_n and the section conjecture holds, (371) has no non-cuspidal splittings.
(2) Conversely, only the 'easy' direction is needed for arithmetic: each Q-point gives a section, distinct from the cuspidal ones. So proving directly that every splitting of (371) is cuspidal would prove Fermat for exponent n, without establishing the anabelian yoga, whose proof 'seems well out of reach'.

He then proposes a strategy: a deep anabelian analysis of M_{0,3} and N_{1,1}. In his notation these are the (S_3-extended) fundamental group of P^1−{0,1,∞} and its genus-1 analogue, the latter related to the modular/Teichmüller group of M_{1,1}; Fermat curves are quotients of modular curves of level 2. Using successively finer 'approximations' of π1(U_n) and of the extension structure (371), the aim is to rule out non-trivial sections for all n ≥ 3. Every refinement of the 'Lie approximations' of M_{0,3} (the nilpotent / Lie-algebra truncations developed in the current section) should prompt a re-examination of the splitting question for (371).

The next page makes this concrete. It uses the richer extension (372) incorporating the S_3-symmetry, 1 → π1(U_{n,Q̄}) → π1(U_n, S_3) → Γ_Q × S_3 → 1, and passes to quotients compatible with the Lie approximation. In other words, it proposes nilpotent-quotient obstructions to sections, applied to the Fermat tower.
errors: No mathematical error, but statement (1) ('Fermat true ⇒ no non-trivial splitting') presupposes the section conjecture; Grothendieck is aware of this, which is precisely why he isolates direction (2).

Direction (2) silently uses that a section coming from a point of U_n(Q) is not conjugate to a cuspidal section. This is true (via the centraliser/inertia characterisation, or injectivity results of Kummer type), but it is not argued on the page.

Whether nilpotent ('Lie') quotients alone can ever suffice to kill all non-cuspidal sections is not addressed. Finite-level or nilpotent obstructions are known to be insufficient in some cases, so the programme is heuristic.

ideas.what: Fermat's Last Theorem for exponent n is equivalent (granting the section conjecture), and implied unconditionally, by the non-existence of non-cuspidal sections of π1(U_n) → Γ_Q for the punctured Fermat curve U_n.
ideas.modern_name: Section conjecture applied to Fermat curves; 'sectional' approach to rational points / non-cuspidal sections
ideas.usually_credited_to: Section conjecture: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings, 1983). Fermat-specific version discussed by Ellenberg (unpublished notes, c. 2000) and Wickelgren, and in Davis–Pries–Stojanoska–Wickelgren (2016-).
ideas.where_published: Section conjecture in the letter to Faltings (1983) and Esquisse; the explicit Fermat formulation is not known to me in his circulated texts.

ideas.what: Characterisation of non-cuspidal sections by triviality of the centraliser of the image of Γ_Q^+ = Ker(cyclotomic character).
ideas.modern_name: Cuspidal vs non-cuspidal sections via inertia/centralisers
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura, Mochizuki, Stix (section-theoretic study of cusps)

ideas.what: Using successively finer Lie (nilpotent/unipotent) approximations of π1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) and of the Fermat tower extension to obstruct sections and thereby prove non-existence of rational points.
ideas.modern_name: Lower-central-series / nilpotent obstructions to sections; nonabelian (Chabauty–Kim) unipotent approach to Diophantine problems
ideas.usually_credited_to: Minhyong Kim (2005, 2009); Coates–Kim (2010, Fermat curves via Selmer varieties); Ellenberg; Wickelgren (2009-2012); Ihara (Galois action on Fermat Jacobians through π1 of P^1−3pts, 1986)

ideas.what: Embedding the extension in a richer one with S_3-symmetry, π1(U_n, S_3) → Γ_Q × S_3, with π1(Û_1, S_3) = M_{0,3}.
ideas.modern_name: Equivariant (orbifold) fundamental group extension of the Fermat tower over M_{0,3}/S_3

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly proposes attacking Fermat's Last Theorem by proving that the only sections of π1(U_n) → Γ_Q (punctured Fermat curve) are cuspidal. He notes this needs only the easy direction of the section conjecture, and suggests doing it via ever finer Lie/nilpotent approximations of π1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) and its genus-1 analogue. This anticipates the programme of nilpotent section obstructions for Fermat curves (Ellenberg, Wickelgren, Davis–Pries–Stojanoska–Wickelgren) and the unipotent Chabauty–Kim approach (Kim, Coates–Kim for Fermat curves) by some 20+ years. Those works do not credit Grothendieck for this specific Fermat/section idea.
missed.quote: si nous arrivons à prouver l'inexistence de scindages de (371) autres que ceux "provenant des pts à l'infini", le th. de Fermat serait prouvé pour U_n, même sans avoir établi le "yoga anabélien"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority point: Grothendieck had already formulated the 'nilpotent obstruction to Fermat points via π1 of P^1−3 points' strategy, which is an active area (Kim's programme; Galois action on homology of Fermat curves). His emphasis on the S_3-equivariant extension (372) and on the genus-1 group N_{1,1} could suggest unexplored equivariant refinements of these obstructions.

missed.claim: The programme of re-examining the splitting question for (371)/(372) at each new level of Lie approximation of M_{0,3} is announced but, on this and the following page, not carried out beyond setting up the quotient extensions.
missed.quote: Chaque nouvel affinement dans les "approximations de Lie" de M_{0,3} devrait amener un réexamen de la situation (371) et de la question de ses scindages
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is the use of the S_3 × Γ_Q-equivariant extension structure to constrain sections. Equivariance is not standardly exploited in existing nilpotent-obstruction computations for Fermat curves.

deep.surprise_reason: The idea itself (section conjecture ⇒ rational-point finiteness/non-existence; nilpotent obstructions) is now well known. What is notable is that Grothendieck, around 1981, explicitly targets FLT via non-cuspidal sections of the Fermat tower and Lie approximations of π1(P^1−3pts). This prefigures Ellenberg/Wickelgren/Kim-type work without being credited, and it sits in a less-circulated part of La Longue Marche.
transcription_corrections: '[?]variations de Lie' should almost certainly read 'approximations de Lie' (consistent with the next page: 'approximations de Lie au moins aussi fines').
'pour U_n, disons' — the parenthetical reads '(pour U_n, disons)'.
'pts à l'infini' — written 'pts à l'infini', i.e. points at infinity / cusps.
